[LFST.9.3.7] **Active compare over both compare-class atoms.** The
byte-compare of [LFST.9.3.1] / [LFST.9.3.6] is **performed by the replayer**, not
merely defined. As replay re-fires the engine at each recorded pump boundary ([LFST.9.2.1],
[RFCS.22]),
each re-derived `CallIssued` **and** `RuleFireAnnotation` atom is captured and byte-compared, in
`seq` order (a two-pointer merge — both streams are `seq`-ordered), against the
recorded atom, failing fast with **`DS_ERR_FS_DIVERGENCE`** ([NERR.13]) at the
first difference. The **structural** checks are part of it: a recorded compare
atom with no re-derived twin (missing), a re-derived atom with no recorded twin
(extra), or a kind/order mismatch is the same Divergence — replay fired a
different rule set — a stronger check than the byte-compare alone. `RuleFireAnnotation`'s
identity `(timetag, rule_name)` ([RFCS.11.2]) is compared too, its `timetag` by
[LFST.9.3.6]'s pairing; its parity with
the bracketed `CallIssued`'s join key ([RFCS.15.2]) is what resolves a recorded `CallIssued`
to its firing. `DS_ERR_FS_DIVERGENCE` is distinct from the `EngineDivergence`
**event** (a callback surface); this is the replay compare verdict.
